Welcome to the official documentation for HyEngine!

New to Harmony?

Provides step-by-step instructions for installing Harmony Engine and creating your first functional project. Jump in and learn the essentials.

Getting Started Editor Design Tool

All of Harmony's tools are wrapped into the HyEditor. From project management, asset pipelines, and scene item creation.

Editor Manual Programming the Game

Understand how Harmony’s runtime API and how it works under the hood. Scene nodes, windows, cameras, input, rendering, the game loop and more.

Engine Manual Learn with Sample Projects

Browse a collection of sample projects demonstrating major features how they work in practice. Each example illustrates practical usage patterns.

docs.title: Editor Manual
docs.text: HyEditor's default window layout.

docs.title: 1️⃣. Project Explorer
docs.text: Open Project's will show up here. You may have multiple Project's open and browsable at once, but only one Project may be 'active' at a given time. All the details are provided in the Project Explorer section.

docs.title: 2️⃣. Asset Manager
docs.text: The currently active Project's Asset Manager. Each tab along the top are the major asset types handled independantly from each other. All the details are provided in the Asset Manager section.

docs.title: 3️⃣. Project Tab Bar
docs.text: All currently open Project Item's from the active Project are shown here. You can cycle between them with Ctrl+Tab and each item has its own Undo/Redo stack.

docs.title: 4️⃣. Project Item Properties
docs.text: Shows all the properties of the currently selected Project Item in the Project Tab Bar. The properties set here set are reflected in the middle render window.

docs.title: 5️⃣. Middle Render Window
docs.text: The currently selected Project Item is previewed here. The renderer used here is the same renderer used in your game, HyEngine. Previews are created by simulating the same load process as well, so it's a WYSIWYG work-flow. Pan the view with WASD or Middle Mouse, and zoom with the Mouse Wheel.

docs.title: 6️⃣. Auxiliary Window
docs.text: The Auxiliary window is contextually used when needed. By default it'll display logs, but when an additional window is needed by the Asset Manager or the Project Item Properties, a new tab along the bottom will appear and be shown. Its visibility can be toggled with Ctrl+Space

docs.title: ▶️Editor Flow
docs.text:
Shows how each section of HyEditor works together.
  1. Open a Project Item from Project Explorer...
  2. Shows up in Project Tab Bar, and when selected...
  3. It will be displayed in the Project Item Properties which...
  4. May reference assets in Asset Manager to...
  5. Show a preview in the Middle Render Window

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Harmony Engine is particularly well-suited for developers who:

  • Want to use a completely free and open-source game engine (MIT)
  • Are building any game in the 2d genre
  • Want a code-first workflow without the overhead of large general-purpose engines.
  • Need builds that are performant, lightweight, and cross-platform (including the web browser with optional WebAssembly deployment)

Itermediate C++ knowledge is recommended, but Harmony is also a great way to learn C/C++ for those with the aptitude.

The Harmony Engine consists of two main projects. The editor tool (HyEditor) that manages projects, assets, and scenes. And the engine itself (HyEngine) which is a static library that links into your game application.

docs.title: First Project
docs.text: Our goal here is to speedrun a simple game to cover Harmony Engine's major features. A crash-course of sorts. It assumes you have already done the steps in the Installation & Setup section.

docs.title: Installation & Setup
docs.text: This guide explains how to install the Harmony Game Engine (HyEngine) and prepare your environment. You can optionally compile the HyEditor or download a prebuilt release. All steps assume a Windows or Linux development environment.

docs.title: ▶️Prerequites
docs.text: Before cloning Harmony Engine or building the editor, ensure the following tools are installed:

docs.title: C++ Toolchain (IDE)
docs.text: Visual Studio 2022/2026 is the recommended development environment on Windows: https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/

docs.title: Git
docs.text:
The Harmony Git repository is referenced in all game projects and builds from source. Harmony also uses Git submodules for its dependencies, so a Git client is required.

Windows: Download Git for Windows: https://git-scm.com/download/win

Linux: Git is typically installed already. If not: sudo apt install git

docs.title: CMake
docs.text:
Harmony Engine uses CMake internally to configure and generate all build files for the engine, editor, and game projects.

  1. Download CMake: https://cmake.org/download/
  2. Ensure you select "Add CMake to system PATH" during installation

docs.title: ▶️Clone Git repository
docs.text:
Clone the Harmony Engine repository and initialize submodules:

git clone https://github.com/GameOverture/HarmonyEngine.git
cd HarmonyEngine
git submodule update --init --recursive

Editor and Engine submodules are found in their respective 'vendor' directories.

Important: Submodules must be initialized or the editor and engine will not build correctly.

docs.title: ▶️Get the Editor
docs.text:
You can either:

  • Download a pre-built Release, or
  • Compile the editor from source

docs.title: Option A - Download a pre-built HyEditor Release
docs.text:
Pre-built binaries are available on the project’s GitHub Releases page: https://github.com/GameOverture/HarmonyEngine/releases/latest

This requires no additional setup beyond installing Git and CMake. Simply download the archive, extract it, and run HyEditor.exe.

You can skip the next section that compiles the editor.

docs.title: Option B - Compile the Editor from source
docs.text:
Compiling HyEditor requires the Qt6 framework. Download the Qt Online Installer (Open Source): https://www.qt.io/download-qt-installer-oss

During installation:

  • Only Qt 6.9.3 has been fully tested.

    Everything should be compatible with Qt5, but you will need to modify the CMakeLists.txt and replace Qt6 -> Qt5 references if you really need to use it

  • Qt must be built for your compiler. For Visual Studio users:

    • Install Qt with MSVC 2022 64-bit
  • You must include:
    • Qt Multimedia (under Additional Libraries)

Building with CMake:

You can build using either the CMake GUI or the command-line.

Using CMake GUI:

  1. Open CMake GUI

  2. Set "Where is the source code:" should be the path to cloned Harmony repository: C:/<path_to_repo>/HarmonyEngine

  3. "Where to build the binaries:" should be the same path + "/build" on the end: C:/<path_to_repo>/HarmonyEngine/build

  4. Press "Configure" button and confirm creating the build directory In the next dialog, choose which IDE to generate in first combo box (Visual Studio 2022, Ninja, etc.)

  5. Set Qt6_DIR to the Qt CMake directory:
-Example-  C:\Qt\6.9.3\msvc2022_64\lib\cmake\Qt6
  1. Press "Configure" again until all red options disappear
  2. Press "Generate" once
  3. Press "Open Project" to open the generated solution (.sln) or navigate to the specified build/ directory

If using Visual Studio, installing Qt Visual Studio Tools extension is recommended for Qt-aware debugging and UI file navigation

docs.title: ▶️Running the Editor for the First Time
docs.text:
Whenever HyEditor launches, it checks whether it can find where the Harmony Engine project is located.

If it's the first time running HyEditor, or it can't find Harmony project location.

In the next dialog, browse to the location of the Harmony Engine project. You should be looking for the root directory of the Git repository. When you find a valid location, the red error bar will disappear and can you press OK. The folder contents will look something like this:

Example of a valid Harmony Engine project location.

When you continue, HyEditor will remember this location, and various other editor preferences in the following location:

WINDOWS uses the registry: \HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Harmony Engine

LINUX stores in: ~/.config/Harmony Engine/

If you ever want to change the Harmony Project location, first close HyEditor. You can delete the old location then reopen HyEditor, or keep the old location and point to a new location by doing Tools -> Change Harmony Location

docs.title: ▶️Uninstalling Harmony Engine
docs.text:
• Remove the editor preferences setting at:

WINDOWS uses the registry: \HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Harmony Engine

LINUX stores in: ~/.config/Harmony Engine/

  • Then simply delete the Harmony repository directory and any HyEditor pre-built release you downloaded.
